## Proof

**Yes, $PAP$ is necessarily finite dimensional.**

Let $A$ be a $C^*$-algebra and let $P \in A$ be a projection ($P = P^* = P^2$) of **finite rank**, i.e., under a faithful $*$-representation $\pi : A \to B(H)$ the operator $\pi(P)$ is a finite-rank projection on the Hilbert space $H$. Set
$$n := \operatorname{rank}(\pi(P)) < \infty, \qquad \text{so that } \pi(P)H \text{ is an } n\text{-dimensional subspace of } H.$$

Consider the corner
$$PAP = \{PaP : a \in A\} \subseteq A.$$
Applying the representation,
$$\pi(PAP) = \pi(P)\,\pi(A)\,\pi(P) \subseteq \pi(P)\,B(H)\,\pi(P).$$

The compressed algebra $\pi(P)B(H)\pi(P)$ consists of operators on $H$ that vanish on $(\pi(P)H)^\perp$ and map $\pi(P)H$ into itself; concretely, the map
$$\pi(P)B(H)\pi(P) \;\longrightarrow\; B\bigl(\pi(P)H\bigr), \qquad \pi(P)T\pi(P) \;\mapsto\; T\big|_{\pi(P)H},$$
is a $*$-isomorphism. Since $\pi(P)H$ is $n$-dimensional,
$$B\bigl(\pi(P)H\bigr) \cong M_n(\mathbb{C}), \qquad \dim_{\mathbb{C}} B\bigl(\pi(P)H\bigr) = n^2 < \infty.$$

Therefore $\pi(PAP)$ is a linear subspace of the finite-dimensional space $M_n(\mathbb{C})$, hence
$$\dim \pi(PAP) \le n^2 < \infty.$$

Because $\pi$ is a faithful (isometric, hence injective) $*$-representation, the linear map
$$PAP \longrightarrow \pi(PAP), \qquad PaP \mapsto \pi(P)\pi(a)\pi(P),$$
is a linear isomorphism onto its image. Consequently
$$\dim PAP = \dim \pi(PAP) \le n^2 < \infty.$$

Thus $PAP$ is finite dimensional. $\blacksquare$

**Remark.** The argument uses only that $P$ has finite rank as an operator; the infinite dimensionality of $A$ is irrelevant to the conclusion. The corner $PAP$ is trapped inside the matrix algebra $B(PH) \cong M_{\operatorname{rank}(P)}(\mathbb{C})$, whose dimension is bounded by $(\operatorname{rank} P)^2$, regardless of how large $A$ itself is.
